orders.judge: Hon'ble Mr. Justice Rajiv Sharma
orders.text:
IN THE HIGH COURT OF UTTARAKHAND AT NAINITAL
Writ Petition No.1845 (SS) of 2012 
Mukesh Bahuguna & others …. Petitioners
Versus 
State of Uttarakhand and others …Respondents 
 
Present: Mr. Manoj Tewari, Senior Advocate assisted by Mr. Alok Mahra, 
Advocate, present for the petitioner. 
Mr. N.P. Shah, learned Standing Counsel present for the 
State/respondent nos. 1 & 2. 
Hon’ble Sudhanshu Dhulia, J. (Oral)
1. In this matter a pure question of law is involved 
which relates to inter se seniority between the Lecturers in 
Government Colleges. The question is whether seniority 
has to be counted from the date of promotions or from the 
date on which such vacancy arose. 
2. The petitioners were appointed as lecturer in 
Government Inter Colleges in the year 2005-06, whereas 
the private respondents who are now shown to be senior to 
the petitioners and who were working as Assistant Teacher 
(L.T. Grade) were promoted as Lecturer in the year 2010-
11. They have been shown senior to the petitioners as 
according to the State-respondents the post on which they 
were promoted fell vacant prior to 2005-06 i.e. prior to the 
date when the petitioners were actually appointed as 
Lecturer. Therefore, the question is as to what should be 
the actual date for determination of seniority in such a 
case. 
3. Notices were served to a large number of such 
lecturers. The petitioners, in any case, impleaded thirty one 
such lecturers to whom notices were issued through 
registered post, acknowledgement of which stands received, 
but no one has put in appearance on behalf of the private  2
respondents. The State, has however filed its counter 
affidavit stating that the private respondents were given 
seniority over the petitioners as the post of lecturers on 
which they were promoted fell vacant prior to the time 
when the petitioners were given appointment. 
4. The petitioners now contend that promotion to 
the post of Principal in Higher Secondary School is under 
consideration and promotions will be made as per the 
seniority, which is presently under challenge. 
5. In view of the fact as stated by the learned Senior 
Advocate Mr. Manoj Tiwari before this Court as well as the 
fact that in spite of service, the private respondents have 
failed to put in their appearance, as an interim measure, it 
is hereby directed that the respondents/State not to give 
effect to the seniority list, which is presently under 
challenge before this Court in the present writ petition, in 
any future promotions. 
6. List this matter after three weeks in daily cause 
list. Private respondents may file their counter affidavits in 
the meanwhile. 
7. Stay application (CLMA) No.14108 of 2012 
stands disposed of. 
 (Sudhanshu Dhulia, J.) 
 30.06.2014 
ML

orders.judge: Hon'ble Mr. Justice Ravindra Maithani
orders.text:
WPSS No. 1845 of 2012
Hon’ble Ravindra Maithani, J.
Mr. K.P. Upadhayay, Sr. Advocate, 
assisted by Mr. Hemant Pant, Advocate for the 
petitioners.
Mr. P.S. Bisht, Addl. C.S.C. for the State.
Mr. S.S. Yadav, Advocate for the 
respondent nos.3 to 63.
Mr. N.S. Pundir, Advocate for respondent 
no.71/Public Service Commission.
In this writ petition, the dispute is with 
regard to inter se seniority between the directly 
appointed Lecturer in the Government Inter 
College and those who were appointed on 
promotion. The writ petition has been filed by 
those Lecturers who were directly appointed. A 
large number of private respondents who were 
appointed on promotion basis have already 
been made party. 
Now, an impeadment application no. 
14109 of 2021 has been moved on behalf of 
the respondents who are appearing in the case 
with the averments therein that almost 3000 
lecturers (between serial number 5154 to 8792 
in the seniority list except those who have 
already retired) would be affected by the 
judgment that may be passed in the instant 
writ petition. Therefore, they all be impleaded 
as party in the instant writ petition
Heard on impleadment application.
Learned counsel for the private 
respondent nos.3 to 63 would submit that the 
affected persons should be made party and 
they should be afforded an opportunity of 
hearing before any order is passed in the 
instant petition. 
On the other hand, learned counsel for 
the petitioners would submit that earlier also, 
a similar kind of impleadment application was 
moved, which was allowed, but, subsequently, 
the Court on 15.10.2019 directed the 
petitioner to make a publication in two 
newspapers having a wide circulation in the 
State of Uttarakhand so as to serve the  affected persons by way of a general notice 
about the pendency of the writ petition before 
this Court. It is argued that the notice was 
duly published and the Court on 06.03.2020 
had already held that the service is sufficient. 
In fact, the notice was published in a 
newspaper on 04.03.2019 which is on record 
alongwith the affidavit of service that has been 
filed by the petitioner. By way of this notice, it 
was informed as hereunder;
“All such regularly promoted lecturers 
(promoted in the year 2010 and 2011) who 
may adversely be affected by the challenge in 
the writ petition are hereby called to appear in 
this Court in person or through counsel duly 
instructed by them on or before 13.11.2019 at 
10:00 o’clock forenoon to answer the petition, 
failing which the said petition shall be heard 
and determined in their absence.
As stated, service by way of this 
publication was held to be sufficient by this 
Court on 06.03.2020. Now, after this 
publication, no question survives for 
impleading any party by the appearing parties. 
Undoubtedly, if any of the affected party comes 
forward to get himself impleaded, that 
application may perhaps be considered, but, 
the application by the private respondent, as 
has been filed, cannot be entertained in view of 
what was ordered by this Court on 15.10.2019 
and what was held on 06.03.2020 after 
publication of the notice in the newspapers. 
Therefore, the impleadment application has no 
merit and it deserves to be dismissed.
The impleadement application is 
dismissed.
Pleadings have already been exchanged.
List this matter in the week commencing 
20.09.2021 for final hearing.
 (Ravindra Maithani, J.) 01.09.2021 Ujjwal

orders.judge: Hon'ble Mr. Justice Ravindra Maithani
orders.text:
WPSS No. 3682 of 2017
With
WPSS No. 1845 of 2012
Hon’ble Ravindra Maithani, J.
Mr. K.P. Upadhyay, Senior Advocate, 
assisted by Mr. Hemant Pant, Advocate for 
the petitioner in WPSS No. 1845 of 2012.
Mr. K.C. Tiwari, Advocate for the 
petitioner in WPSS No. 3682 of 2017.
Mr. P.C. Bisht, Additional C.S.C. for 
the State.
Mr. S.S. Yadav, Advocate for the 
respondent nos. 3 to 63.
This case relates to inter se seniority 
of Lecturers. It is between two groups, one, 
those who were promoted from Assistant 
Teacher, LT Grade and those, who were 
directly appointed.
It is the case of the petitioners that 
pursuant to the requisition and an 
advertisement of the year 2003, they 
appeared in the examination for appointment 
to the post of Lecturer and were appointed 
between 10.10.2005 and 20.11.2006. Till 
then, there was no dispute. It so happened 
that in the year 2010 and 2011, the 
Department sent a requisition to the 
Uttarakhand Public Service Commission for 
promotional exercise to the post of Lecturer 
and promotion orders were issued on 
06.08.2010 and 20.07.2011. It was with 
regard to the requisition sent on 30.03.2010 
and 25.04.2011 respectively.
The grievance of the petitioners begin 
from the point, when it is stated that the 
persons appointed by promotion were given 
seniority from some year prior to the
appointment of the petitioners, thereby 
placing the petitioners below such Lecturers, 
who were promoted in the year 2010 and 
2010.
It is the case of respondent no.2 on 
behalf of the State that the Assistant  Teachers, who were working as the Assistant 
Teachers, L.T. Grade were temporarily 
promoted on the post of Lecturers pursuant 
to the applicable Rules and prior to that they 
were already working, as Lecturer on adhoc 
basis, pursuant to their adhoc promotion 
made between 2001 and 2007.
During the course of argument, 
learned counsel for the petitioners raised the 
following arguments:-
(i) All the Lecturers, who were 
appointed by way of promotion on 
06.08.2010 and 22.07.2011 were 
not earlier working as adhoc 
Lecturers. Some of them were 
working as adhoc Lecturers, but 
some of them were appointed for 
the first time as Lecturers;
(ii) Some of the Lecturers, who were 
promoted in the year 2010 and 
2011, even did not have the 
requisite educational qualification 
of post graduation in the 
particular subject when they were 
promoted as adhod Lecturer
and/or;
(iii) The period for which, the adhoc
Lecturer had worked cannot be 
counted for the purpose of their 
seniority because there 
appointment as an adhoc Lecturer 
was not as per Rule 16 of the 
1992 applicable Rules.
When asked, learned State counsel is 
not in a position to tell these things. There is 
no specific denial of the averments as made 
in para 22 of the writ petition with regard to 
the status of the adhoc Lecturers. Therefore, 
the Court directs the respondent no.2 to file a 
counter affidavit giving the following details:-
(i) How many Lecturers were 
appointed by way of promotion in  the year 2010 and 2011. Alongwith 
it a breakup should given as to 
how many of them had already
been working as adhoc Lecturers?
(ii) How such adhoc Lecturers were 
appointed as adhoc Lecturers? 
What procedure was adopted? If 
more than one procedure was 
adopted, the procedure that was 
adopted with regard to the number 
of candidates should be revealed 
and;
(iii)Whether all such Lecturers, who 
had been working as adhoc 
Lecturer prior to their appointment 
as Lecturer in the years 2010 and 
2011 had the requisite 
qualification of Post Graduation 
when they were appointed as 
adhoc Lecturer?
Let a short affidavit be filed by the 
State within next four weeks to explain their 
point.
During the course of argument, Mr. 
K.C. Tiwari, learned counsel for the petitioner 
submits that similar matters were also 
decided by this Court which are Writ Petition 
(S/S) No. 1796 of 2012 and Special Appeal
No.248 of 2015.
List in the week commencing 
15.11.2021 alongwith Writ Petition (S/S) No. 
1796 of 2012 and Special Appeal No.248 of 
2015.
 (Ravindra Maithani, J.)
 08.10.2021 Jitendra
